title: DSA - Merge Sort
description:
## Merge Sort
Merge sort uses **divide and conquer**:
1. Split the array in half
2. Recursively sort each half
3. Merge the two sorted halves together

### Visualization:
```
[5, 3, 8, 1]
   /       \
[5, 3]   [8, 1]      <- split
 /  \     /  \
[5] [3] [8] [1]      <- split again
 \  /     \  /
[3, 5]   [1, 8]      <- merge (sorted)
   \       /
[1, 3, 5, 8]         <- merge (sorted)
```

**Big O: O(n log n)** - always. Best, worst, average. Way faster than bubble sort.

---
## Assignment:
Implement `mergeSort` that takes a `std::vector<int>` and returns a sorted `std::vector<int>`.

### Steps:
- [ ] Base case: if array size <= 1, return it
- [ ] Split array into left and right halves using `std::vector<int>(arr.begin(), arr.begin() + mid)` syntax
- [ ] Recursively call `mergeSort` on both halves
- [ ] Create a `merge` helper that takes two sorted vectors and returns one sorted vector:
  - [ ] Create an empty result vector
  - [ ] Use two index variables `i` and `j` starting at 0
  - [ ] While both indexes are in bounds, compare `left[i]` and `right[j]`, push the smaller one
  - [ ] Push any remaining elements from whichever side isn't empty
  - [ ] Return the merged result
- [ ] Call your `merge` helper on the two sorted halves and return it
